entries.title: DNS name resolution timed out
entries.what: None of the configured DNS servers answered for a name. Occasional timeouts are normal; many mean DNS or connectivity problems.
causes: Name only resolvable inside a VPN
fix: Check the DNS servers: ipconfig /all
Test: nslookup <name> <dns-server>
Harmless if rare and the internet works

entries.title: Dynamic DNS registration failed
entries.what: The computer could not register its name/address in DNS. Other computers may not find it by name.
causes: DNS server does not accept dynamic updates
No permission on the DNS zone
fix: In a domain: check that the DNS server is a domain DNS and the zone allows secure updates
At home: harmless, routers usually don't accept registrations

entries.title: No IP address from DHCP
entries.what: The network adapter did not get an IP address from a DHCP server.
fix: ipconfig /release and /renew
Check the router/DHCP server and its address pool
Check cable/switch port

entries.title: Could not renew IP address
entries.what: The adapter could not renew its DHCP lease.
fix: Check connectivity to the DHCP server; renew with ipconfig /renew

entries.title: IP address conflict
entries.what: Another device on the network uses the same IP address. Both may lose connectivity.
causes: Static IP that is also in the DHCP pool
Two devices configured with the same static IP
fix: Find the other device by the MAC address in the message (arp -a, router's client list)
Use DHCP reservations instead of static IPs inside the pool

entries.title: TCP port reuse limit hit
entries.what: TCP could not open an outgoing connection because local ports were recently used - sign of port exhaustion.
causes: A program opening huge numbers of connections
Very short-lived connections at high rate
fix: Find the program: netstat -ano | find /c "TIME_WAIT"
Update or fix the application; increase dynamic port range if needed

entries.title: Ephemeral port exhaustion
entries.what: TCP/IP could not allocate an outgoing port; all ephemeral ports are in use. New connections fail.
fix: netstat -ano to find the process with most connections; restart/fix it

entries.title: NetBIOS name conflict
entries.what: The computer's NetBIOS name is already used by another device on the network.
causes: Two computers with the same name
fix: Rename one of the computers

entries.title: Network link down (Intel)
entries.what: The Intel network adapter lost its link.
fix: Check cable and switch port
Disable 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power' for the adapter

entries.title: Network link down (Intel)
entries.what: The Intel network adapter lost its link.
fix: Check cable and switch port
Disable adapter power saving

entries.title: Network link down (Intel)
entries.what: The Intel network adapter lost its link.
fix: Check cable and switch port
Disable adapter power saving

entries.title: Network link up (Intel)
entries.what: The Intel network adapter established a link.

entries.title: Time sync source set
entries.what: The time service is now synchronizing with the time source in the message.

entries.title: Receiving valid time
entries.what: The time provider is now receiving valid time data.

entries.title: Time not synchronized for a long time
entries.what: The computer clock has not been synchronized for longer than expected.
fix: w32tm /resync
w32tm /query /status
Allow UDP 123 to the time source

entries.title: Cannot find domain time source
entries.what: The NTP client could not find a domain controller to sync time with. Kerberos fails if the clock drifts more than 5 minutes.
causes: No connection to a domain controller (VPN off, offline)
fix: Check DC connectivity and DNS
w32tm /resync /rediscover

entries.title: Cannot resolve the NTP server name
entries.what: The time service could not resolve the configured NTP server.
fix: Check: w32tm /query /peers
Harmless once at boot if it syncs later

entries.title: Time service stopped advertising
entries.what: This machine stopped acting as a time source because its own clock is not synchronized. Important on domain controllers.
causes: PDC emulator has no reliable external time source
fix: Configure the PDC emulator with external NTP servers: w32tm /config /manualpeerlist:... /syncfromflags:manual /reliable:yes /update

entries.title: No domain controller available
entries.what: The computer could not set up a secure session with a domain controller.
causes: Network not ready at boot (common on Wi-Fi)
DNS not pointing to domain DNS servers
fix: Harmless once at boot if logons work
Check that DNS points to domain DNS servers
Test: nltest /sc_query:<domain>

entries.title: Failed to authenticate with the domain controller
entries.what: The computer's secure channel with the domain is broken (machine account password mismatch).
causes: Computer restored from an old snapshot/backup
Machine account reset or duplicated name
fix: Test-ComputerSecureChannel -Repair -Credential (Get-Credential)
Or rejoin the domain

entries.title: Computer failed to authenticate (DC side)
entries.what: On a domain controller: a computer failed to authenticate because of its account/password.
fix: Repair or rejoin the named computer

entries.title: No trust account for computer
entries.what: On a domain controller: a computer tried to connect but its account does not exist.
fix: Rejoin the computer to the domain

entries.title: DC DNS records not registered
entries.what: A domain controller could not register its DNS records.
causes: DNS server unreachable or not allowing updates
fix: Check DNS on the DC; run dcdiag /test:dns

entries.title: Clients from subnets without a site
entries.what: Clients connected from IP subnets not mapped to an AD site. Logon may use a distant DC.
causes: Missing subnet definitions in AD Sites and Services
fix: Add the subnets from netlogon.log to AD Sites and Services

entries.title: Group Policy failed: no DC connection
entries.what: Group Policy processing failed because the network/DC was not reachable.
fix: Harmless once at boot; gpupdate /force later should succeed

entries.title: Group Policy extension failed
entries.what: A Group Policy client-side extension (e.g. Drive Maps, Registry, Scheduled Tasks) failed to apply settings.
fix: Run gpresult /h report.html and check the named extension

entries.title: Group Policy could not read registry.pol
entries.what: A Group Policy registry file is corrupted.
fix: Delete C:\Windows\System32\GroupPolicy\Machine\registry.pol and run gpupdate /force

entries.title: Group Policy could not read gpt.ini
entries.what: The computer could not read a GPO file from SYSVOL.
fix: Check access to \\domain\SYSVOL
Check SYSVOL replication on the domain controllers

entries.title: Group Policy could not resolve the user name
entries.what: Group Policy failed to identify the user or computer in the domain.
fix: Check connectivity to the domain

entries.title: Group Policy query failed
entries.what: Querying the list of Group Policy objects failed.
fix: Check connectivity to the domain

entries.title: Group Policy applied
entries.what: Group Policy settings were processed successfully.

entries.title: Group Policy applied
entries.what: Group Policy settings were processed successfully.

entries.title: Kerberos ticket error (wrong account for SPN)
entries.what: A Kerberos ticket was encrypted for a different account than expected - usually a duplicate or misplaced SPN.
causes: Service running under a different account
DNS pointing a name to the wrong server
fix: Find duplicates: setspn -X
Check the DNS record for the server name in the message

entries.title: KDC: no suitable key for encryption type
entries.what: The domain controller could not issue a ticket because no key with a supported encryption type exists for the account.
causes: Old account password set before AES was enabled
RC4 disabled while accounts only have RC4 keys
fix: Reset the account's password
Review allowed Kerberos encryption types

entries.title: KDC: encryption type not supported
entries.what: A ticket request used an encryption type the account does not support.
fix: Review msDS-SupportedEncryptionTypes and policy

entries.title: TLS: cannot access the certificate's private key
entries.what: Schannel could not use the private key of a TLS server certificate. TLS connections to this machine may fail.
causes: Missing permissions on the MachineKeys folder
Certificate imported without its private key
fix: Check the certificate in certlm.msc has a private key
Check permissions on C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Crypto\RSA\MachineKeys

entries.title: TLS: no common cipher suite
entries.what: A client tried to connect over TLS but none of its cipher suites are supported by this server.
fix: Identify the client; update it, or review enabled cipher suites

entries.title: TLS: fatal alert received
entries.what: The remote side ended a TLS connection with an alert. Very common and usually harmless (closed tabs, scanners, cert checks).

entries.title: TLS: fatal alert generated
entries.what: This machine ended a TLS connection with an alert. Very common and usually harmless.

entries.title: TLS: fatal error creating credentials
entries.what: Schannel could not create TLS client/server credentials.
fix: Check machine certificates and TLS protocol settings

entries.title: RDP protocol error from a client
entries.what: The Remote Desktop server got an invalid packet from a client. Often internet scanners probing port 3389.
fix: If RDP is exposed to the internet, put it behind a VPN or RD Gateway

entries.title: RDP protocol error (X.224)
entries.what: An RDP connection had a protocol error. Often scanners or interrupted connections.
fix: If RDP is exposed to the internet, restrict it

entries.title: RDP user authenticated (network level)
entries.what: A user passed network-level authentication for Remote Desktop. The message shows the user and source address.

entries.title: Session logon succeeded
entries.what: A user logged on to a session (local or Remote Desktop). The message shows user and source address.

entries.title: Session logoff
entries.what: A user logged off from a session.

entries.title: Session disconnected
entries.what: A session was disconnected (user closed RDP window or lost connection).

entries.title: Session reconnected
entries.what: A user reconnected to an existing session.

entries.title: Connected to Wi-Fi
entries.what: The computer connected to a wireless network.

entries.title: Disconnected from Wi-Fi
entries.what: The computer disconnected from a wireless network. The message gives the reason.
fix: If frequent: update the Wi-Fi driver; disable adapter power saving

entries.title: Wi-Fi connection failed
entries.what: Connecting to a wireless network failed. The message gives the reason.
fix: Read the failure reason in the message
